default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-188.title: Decoupled-tape micro-break fade
E-188.hypothesis: WIN and WDO normally move against each other because foreign flow trades both; when the rolling correlation of their 1-bar returns is no longer clearly negative, the index tape is local churn without macro flow, so a close beyond the last 10 minutes' high/low is a small local push that liquidity providers lean back; fade it.

E-189.title: PTAX-window index spill fade
E-189.hypothesis: During the four 10-minute PTAX consultation windows (10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 13:00) dealers push the dollar for the fixing and foreign desks hedge index exposure mechanically, so a WIN move made inside the window is fixing-related flow, not information; once the window closes that flow stops, so fade the window move.

E-190.title: Change-of-character counter bar follow
E-190.hypothesis: After a move larger than usual for the window, a counter bar whose body is larger than ANY trend-direction body of the window shows the counter side now trades with more urgency than the trend side ever did (Wyckoff change of character); the trend holders are no longer the strongest flow, so follow the counter bar.

E-191.title: Two-close volume acceptance break follow
E-191.hypothesis: Market Profile traders treat a single close beyond a range as a probe and two consecutive closes beyond it as acceptance; when both closes also trade at least normal volume for their minute, the new prices are being accepted by real participation rather than a stop sweep, so responsive traders give up and the move extends.

E-192.title: Chandelier-stop sweep fade
E-192.hypothesis: Many trend followers trail stops at the chandelier level (recent high minus m x ATR); a close through it fills that whole cluster of forced sell orders at once, and once the stop flow is spent nobody is left to sell, so liquidity providers who absorbed it lean the price back; buy the sweep (mirror at the short stop).

E-193.title: Volume-clock milestone momentum
E-193.hypothesis: Execution algorithms schedule parent orders against the expected daily volume curve and check progress at volume milestones; when the session crosses each fixed share of a typical day's volume while the day has already moved more than usual from the open, the scheduled remainder of those orders pushes the same way.

E-194.title: Dollar-jump index overreaction fade
E-194.hypothesis: When the dollar jumps in one bar, index algorithms re-price WIN off it mechanically and overshoot; a WIN bar moving the opposite way much more than usual for its minute in the same bar is that mechanical repricing, and once the dollar news is absorbed local liquidity providers lean it back; fade the WIN reaction bar.

E-195.title: MFI failure swing
E-195.hypothesis: Wilder-style failure swing on the volume-weighted Money Flow Index: after money flow was overbought, a bounce that fails below the level and then breaks the prior MFI reaction low shows buying volume drying up on each attempt; the volume-backed buyers have left and the price follows the money flow down (mirror for oversold).

E-196.title: Decaying-volatility micro-break fade
E-196.hypothesis: When the recent bar ranges have shrunk well below those of the window before, the active flow of the earlier window is finished and market makers are re-centering their quotes; a close beyond the last 15 minutes' high/low in that state is a leftover push with no initiator behind it, so fade it.

E-197.title: Balanced-flow micro-break fade
E-197.hypothesis: When volume on up bars and down bars over the window nearly cancel, aggressive buyers and sellers are trading against each other with no net side; a close beyond the last 15 minutes' high/low in that balance is not backed by net flow and is reabsorbed by the other side, so fade it.
